speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing double vision, difficulty climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness. To better understand your condition, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if they are constant or intermittent?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The key features of symptoms worsening with activity (fatigability) and improving with rest, combined with ocular (double vision) and limb weakness without sensory or balance issues, are classic for this neuromuscular junction disorder. I would like to confirm this with antibody testing and a chest X-ray to rule out thymoma. REQUEST TEST: Anti-AChR Antibodies, Anti-MuSK Antibodies; REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.
